---
title: "check-contour-3d.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags a contour or level-curve plot
with no 3D surface plot of the same function.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-11-03) is that every contour plot
of a function of two variables gets a matching 3D surface plot.
This implements
[gha#1443](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1443).
It warns by default while the notes repositories catch up.

A contour call, inside a code fence, is one of these:

- `geom_contour`, `geom_contour_filled`, `stat_contour`;
- plotly's `add_contour` or `type = "contour"`;
- base R's `contour(` and `filled.contour(`;
- matplotlib's `.contour(` and `.contourf(`;
- `Plot.contour`.

A file is satisfied when any of these holds:

- it holds a 3D call in a code fence
  (`add_surface`, `plot_surface`, `plot_trisurf`, `persp`, `type = "surface"`);
- it includes a 3D figure subfile (`{{< include ..._3d.qmd >}}` or `...-3d.qmd`);
- a sibling subfile named `<stem>-3d.qmd` sits beside it;
- it holds an HTML comment `<!-- no-3d: reason -->` with a non-empty reason,
  for a contour plot that is not of a function of two variables,
  such as a density estimated from data.

Use `paths-ignore` to exempt whole paths.
The test is per file, so a file with two contour figures and one 3D plot passes.
Put each figure in its own subfile to get a per-figure test.

## Scope

Only a contour figure whose code fence holds a line a pull request adds is reported,
so existing figures are never reflagged.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new, and a blank added line is not content.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file on purpose,
which measures how many existing contour figures lack a 3D plot.
Every run prints how many lines, files, and contour figures it examined.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default       | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd'`     | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`          | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `false`       | Fail the workflow when a contour plot has no 3D plot. The default is warning annotations only. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`       | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`      | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-contour-3d.yml in your repo.
name: Check contour 3D plots

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-contour-3d.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   fail: true         # block on a finding (defaults to false)
```
